grid.teamDesc: Cadillac Racing represented General Motors' return to top-level prototype endurance racing with the all-new Cadillac V-Series.R. The program combined decades of American motorsport engineering experience with global endurance racing ambitions, competing against the world's leading manufacturers in the Hypercar category. Backed directly by Cadillac and operated with factory support, the team quickly established itself as a serious challenger for podiums and victories in the FIA World Endurance Championship.

Ferrari AF Corse represented Ferrari's long-awaited return to endurance racing's top category after fifty years away from the premier prototype class. Partnering with AF Corse, one of the most successful GT racing organizations in modern motorsport, Ferrari developed the 499P Hypercar to compete for overall victories at Le Mans and in the FIA World Endurance Championship. The project instantly became one of the sport's most significant factory programs.

Ferrari AF Corse represented Ferrari's long-awaited return to endurance racing's top category after fifty years away from the premier prototype class. Partnering with AF Corse, one of the most successful GT racing organizations in modern motorsport, Ferrari developed the 499P Hypercar to compete for overall victories at Le Mans and in the FIA World Endurance Championship. The project instantly became one of the sport's most significant factory programs.

Glickenhaus Racing embodied the independent spirit of endurance racing through its bespoke 007 LMH Hypercar program. Founded by entrepreneur and automotive enthusiast Jim Glickenhaus, the team sought to compete directly against major global manufacturers using a purpose-built racing prototype. Despite operating with significantly smaller resources than many rivals, Glickenhaus earned widespread respect for taking on the sport's largest brands at the highest level.

Peugeot TotalEnergies marked the French manufacturer's return to top-flight endurance racing with the radical Peugeot 9X8 Hypercar. Designed with innovative engineering concepts and supported by multinational energy partner TotalEnergies, the program represented Peugeot's ambition to challenge for overall victories on the world stage. The team combined factory resources, technological innovation, and experienced drivers in pursuit of endurance racing success.

Peugeot TotalEnergies marked the French manufacturer's return to top-flight endurance racing with the radical Peugeot 9X8 Hypercar. Designed with innovative engineering concepts and supported by multinational energy partner TotalEnergies, the program represented Peugeot's ambition to challenge for overall victories on the world stage. The team combined factory resources, technological innovation, and experienced drivers in pursuit of endurance racing success.

Porsche Penske Motorsport united one of the most successful sports car manufacturers in history with the championship-winning expertise of Team Penske. Created to lead Porsche's global prototype racing effort, the operation brought together elite engineering, operational excellence, and decades of endurance racing success. The Porsche 963 was developed to continue the brand's legacy of overall victories at the world's most prestigious endurance events.

Porsche Penske Motorsport united one of the most successful sports car manufacturers in history with the championship-winning expertise of Team Penske. Created to lead Porsche's global prototype racing effort, the operation brought together elite engineering, operational excellence, and decades of endurance racing success. The Porsche 963 was developed to continue the brand's legacy of overall victories at the world's most prestigious endurance events.

Hertz Team JOTA was one of endurance racing's most accomplished independent organizations, known for consistently outperforming expectations against factory-backed rivals. Running a customer Porsche 963, the team combined elite operational execution, strategic expertise, and a proven record of success in prototype racing. The partnership between JOTA, Porsche, and title sponsor Hertz created one of the strongest privateer efforts on the Hypercar grid.

Proton Competition is one of Germany's most respected endurance racing organizations and has enjoyed a long relationship with Porsche in international sports car racing. As the first customer Porsche 963 operation in the WEC Hypercar era, the team demonstrated the viability of privateer participation at the highest level while leveraging decades of experience in endurance competition.

Toyota Gazoo Racing entered 2023 as the benchmark organization in endurance racing after multiple world championships and Le Mans victories. The GR010 Hybrid showcased Toyota's advanced hybrid technology and extensive motorsport expertise developed through years of competition at the highest level. With a factory-backed operation and world-class driver lineup, the team remained the standard by which every Hypercar competitor was measured.

Toyota Gazoo Racing entered 2023 as the benchmark organization in endurance racing after multiple world championships and Le Mans victories. The GR010 Hybrid showcased Toyota's advanced hybrid technology and extensive motorsport expertise developed through years of competition at the highest level. With a factory-backed operation and world-class driver lineup, the team remained the standard by which every Hypercar competitor was measured.

Floyd Vanwall Racing Team revived one of motorsport's most historic names through the Vanwall Vandervell 680 Hypercar program. The project sought to reintroduce the legendary British marque to top-level endurance racing while competing against well-funded factory manufacturers. With experienced international drivers and a distinctive independent spirit, the team became one of the most unique entries on the 2023 grid.

ORT by TF Sport has grown into one of Aston Martin’s most trusted endurance racing partners, earning victories and championships through consistent performances on some of the world’s toughest circuits. Campaigning the Aston Martin Vantage GTE, the British squad blends technical precision, experienced personnel, and a racer-first mentality that has made it a fixture at the front of GT competition. For drivers seeking a team that combines proven results with a family atmosphere and unwavering determination, ORT by TF Sport represents an ideal platform for success.

NorthWest AMR proudly represents Aston Martin’s enduring presence in international GT racing, bringing together experienced personnel and competitive drivers under one of the sport’s most iconic brands. Operating the Aston Martin Vantage GTE, the team embraces the challenge of endurance racing with determination, professionalism, and a commitment to continuous improvement. For competitors seeking a team built upon tradition, resilience, and ambition, NorthWest AMR offers the chance to race beneath the wings of a legendary manufacturer.

D'Station Racing has become a fan favorite through its unique identity, international presence, and long-standing partnership with Aston Martin. The Japanese team has steadily developed into a respected contender in endurance racing, combining disciplined preparation with a never-quit attitude. Racing the Aston Martin Vantage GTE, D'Station provides drivers an opportunity to represent one of Asia’s most recognizable GT programs while competing on the world’s biggest endurance racing stages.

Corvette Racing stands as one of the most iconic factory-backed programs in endurance racing history, with decades of success at Le Mans, Sebring, Daytona, and beyond. Operating the fearsome Corvette C8.R, the American squad is renowned for meticulous preparation, engineering excellence, and an unmatched commitment to performance. Built upon a legacy of victories against the world's best manufacturers, Corvette Racing offers competitors the opportunity to wear one of motorsport’s most respected badges while pursuing glory on racing’s biggest stages.

AF Corse is one of endurance racing’s most legendary organizations, having built its reputation through championship-winning campaigns with Ferrari across GT and prototype competition. Fielding the Ferrari 488 GTE Evo, the Italian powerhouse combines elite engineering, strategic excellence, and decades of Le Mans experience into a package capable of competing for victories at every level of endurance racing. With a culture built around professionalism and success, AF Corse offers drivers the opportunity to join one of motorsport’s most respected and accomplished teams while continuing a legacy defined by trophies, teamwork, and relentless pursuit of excellence.

AF Corse’s No. 54 operation continues the team’s tradition of excellence, providing a competitive environment where experienced racers and rising talent come together under one of Ferrari’s most successful customer programs. Backed by world-class engineering and championship-caliber strategy, the Ferrari 488 GTE Evo remains a formidable contender throughout the endurance racing calendar. Drivers joining this effort become part of a team whose expectations are simple: compete hard, perform consistently, and challenge for victory whenever the opportunity arises.

Kessel Racing has spent years establishing itself as one of Ferrari’s most recognizable customer teams, earning success across a wide range of GT championships and endurance events. Behind the wheel of the Ferrari 488 GTE Evo, the Swiss-based operation pairs technical experience with a passion for competition that has become its trademark. Known for professionalism, consistency, and an unwavering love of racing, Kessel Racing gives drivers the opportunity to join a respected organization that continues to challenge for top results around the world.

Richard Mille AF Corse unites the championship-winning expertise of AF Corse with the prestige and ambition associated with one of motorsport’s most recognizable premium partners. Racing the Ferrari 488 GTE Evo, the team benefits from elite resources, experienced personnel, and a proven ability to challenge at the front of the field. Combining performance, professionalism, and a relentless desire to win, Richard Mille AF Corse offers drivers the chance to join an operation where expectations are high and success is always the target.

Project 1 - AO Racing combines German endurance racing expertise with an ambitious competitive spirit that has earned respect throughout international GT competition. Racing the Porsche 911 RSR-19, the team embraces Porsche’s rich motorsport heritage while developing its own reputation for resilience and determination. Whether fighting through difficult races or capitalizing on race-winning opportunities, Project 1 - AO delivers an environment where commitment and teamwork are rewarded with the chance to compete against the very best in endurance racing.

Iron Lynx rapidly emerged as one of endurance racing’s premier GT organizations, building a reputation through major victories, championship fights, and strong manufacturer partnerships. Campaigning the Porsche 911 RSR-19, the team brings together elite engineering talent, innovative preparation, and a relentless competitive mentality. For racers looking to compete within a modern organization committed to growth and success, Iron Lynx offers a chance to be part of a team constantly pushing toward the next milestone.

Dempsey-Proton Racing has become synonymous with Porsche endurance racing, combining decades of experience with a reputation for extracting maximum performance from every program it undertakes. Long respected throughout Le Mans and world championship competition, the team thrives on discipline, preparation, and race-day execution. Joining Dempsey-Proton means becoming part of a storied organization that values commitment, rewards consistency, and embraces the challenge of competing at the highest level of GT racing.

Iron Dames has become one of motorsport’s most inspirational and recognizable projects, demonstrating that ambition, talent, and determination can break barriers on the world stage. Competing with the Porsche 911 RSR-19, the team has earned admiration throughout endurance racing while consistently fighting for strong results against established rivals. More than simply a racing team, Iron Dames represents a movement driven by passion, opportunity, and excellence, making it one of the most exciting programs in international motorsport.

GR Racing has built its reputation through perseverance, professionalism, and a deep passion for endurance competition. Running the Ferrari 488 GTE Evo, the team consistently punches above its weight by maximizing opportunities and delivering strong performances against larger organizations. With a culture centered on teamwork and continuous improvement, GR Racing provides drivers the opportunity to join a close-knit group committed to competing with heart, determination, and pride.

Proton Competition is among the most respected names in Porsche customer racing, with years of success spanning endurance championships and multiple appearances at the 24 Hours of Le Mans. Fielding the Porsche 911 RSR-19, the German squad combines technical expertise, race-winning experience, and one of the strongest support structures in GT racing. Drivers joining Proton Competition become part of an organization that understands what it takes to succeed on the global stage and possesses the tools necessary to compete for top honors.

stories.title: Southern California Twilight: Buemi Steals Long Beach as Mann Masters GTE Chaos
stories.standfirst: Under the golden Pacific twilight, Sébastien Buemi turned late-race precision into victory while Simon Mann conquered an attritional street brawl.
stories.body:
The sun dipped toward the Pacific, casting long, amber shadows across the concrete canyons of Long Beach, but the evening air provided no relief from the brutal intensity of street racing. An eighty-minute endurance contest pinned between uncompromising concrete barriers is an unforgiving test of nerve. One slight twitch of the wheel or a lapse in focus around the Seaside Way fountain, and the walls take their toll. Round 2 of the championship delivered breathtaking drama, unexpected heartbreak, and a masterful showcase of composure in both classes.

## Buemi Strikes Late as Cameron's Dominance Unravels

For nearly the entire race, **Dane Cameron** looked entirely untouchable. Launching from the outside of the front row in the No. 5 Porsche Penske Motorsport 963, Cameron executed a brilliant opening move to jump pole-sitter **Sébastien Buemi** on the run to Turn 1. From there, Cameron settled into a relentless rhythm, clicking off pristine laps and pacing the Hypercar field for 44 of the 60 laps.

Behind him, Buemi refused to crack. The Toyota GR010 Hybrid stayed glued within striking distance through the first round of scheduled fuel-and-tyre stops on lap 24. While Tom Dillmann stretched his opening stint in the Vanwall to briefly inherit the lead, Cameron reclaimed control once the cycle leveled out. Yet the race swung on the execution of the final pit sequence. When Cameron dove into the pit lane on lap 48 for his second scheduled service, Buemi stayed out, extracting maximum pace before peeling in. Thanks to a razor-sharp 86-second turnaround from the Toyota Gazoo Racing crew, Buemi rejoined with superior momentum, took the lead on lap 52 as the alternative strategies washed out, and surged away.

Buemi punctuated his masterclass by posting the fastest lap of the race at 1:15.550, crossing the bricks 5.041 seconds clear of Cameron to bag a maximum haul of 52 points. Kévin Estre completed the podium in the No. 6 Porsche (+10.850s), holding off Round 1 winner Mike Conway in fourth (+11.322s). Round 1 pole-sitter Antonio Fuoco had to settle for fifth in the No. 50 Ferrari 499P, trailing by 13.912 seconds, while Earl Bamber took sixth for Cadillac. With that victory, Buemi vaults to the summit of the Hypercar standings with 64 points, dislodging Conway, who now sits on 50.

## Heartbreak for Iron Dames and Aston Martin

If Hypercar was an exercise in strategic precision, LMGTE was pure, unfiltered attrition. Axcil Jefferies gave Northwest AMR the upper hand in qualifying, claiming pole with a searing 1:21.276. For the opening 30 laps, Jefferies controlled the tempo with authority, keeping a snarling pack of Aston Martins, Porsches, and Ferraris in his rearview mirror.

Then came the pit-stop window, and the street circuit showed its teeth. On lap 31, proton Competition's Harry Tincknell saw his race end violently against the barrier, triggering a devastating DNF for the No. 88 Porsche. Jefferies also suffered on strategy, forced into a two-stop sequence that ruined his shot at victory and relegated him to seventh. 

That opened the door for **Sarah Bovy** and the Iron Dames. Wheeling the pink No. 85 Porsche 911 RSR-19 with surgical flair, Bovy took command on lap 37 and led 19 consecutive laps, looking destined to write championship history. But the streets of Long Beach rarely permit fairy-tale endings. Cruelly, with just two laps remaining, Bovy was forced into pit lane for fuel, only to suffer a terminal DNF on lap 56 that robbed the Iron Dames of a deserved triumph.

## The AF Corse Coup and Catsburg's Charge

Waiting to capitalize on the front-running chaos was **Simon Mann** in the No. 21 AF Corse Ferrari 488 GTE Evo. Mann drove an exceptionally measured race. Sticking to a disciplined, single-stop strategy on lap 36, Mann let the frantic battles ahead burn themselves out. When Bovy dropped out, Mann seized the lead with calm authority, guiding his Ferrari home to capture a stunning 50-point victory.

Behind him, AF Corse celebrated an emphatic team showing, with Thomas Flohr claiming third (+17.050s) and Luis Perez Companc taking fourth (+21.705s). The sole interloper on the podium was championship leader **Nicky Catsburg**. Starting way down in 12th on the GTE grid, Catsburg carved through the carnage with surgical racecraft in the No. 33 Corvette C8.R. His clinical drive earned him second place, just 14.167 seconds behind Mann. The runner-up finish nets Catsburg 36 points, keeping him atop the GTE table with 63 points, while Mann leaps into second on 56.

## Bruised But Unbroken: Powers's Gritty Point

Among the evening's most dramatic personal odysseys was that of **Max Powers** in the No. 57 Kessel Racing Ferrari. Starting from 13th in GTE, Powers unleashed jaw-dropping early pace. Slicing through traffic, he set the outright fastest lap of the class with a blistering 1:21.830 and had climbed all the way up to sixth by lap 13.

However, dancing on the absolute limit along the concrete barriers carries immense danger. At minute 23, Powers suffered a bone-jarring 2,975-severity impact with the wall, inflicting heavy suspension damage. A lengthy 120-second pit stop on lap 17 plunged him to the tail of the field. 

Refusing to retire the wounded machine, Powers battled on. Even after absorbing two further suspension-damaging wall impacts at minutes 63 and 79, plus receiving 17 track limit warnings as he wrestled the car, the Kessel driver refused to concede. Crossing the line two laps down in 12th, Powers was rewarded for his sheer defiance with a hard-earned single championship point, taking his season tally to 16 points and holding seventh in the GTE championship. It was a bruised, battered evening, but Powers showed genuine fighting spirit.

The championship now packs its freight and heads across the Atlantic to the historic asphalt of Italy, where the rolling hills and deep curbs of the Autodromo Internazionale Enzo e Dino Ferrari await.

stories.title: Conway's Late Ambush and Catsburg's Masterclass Ignite Portimão
stories.standfirst: Toyota pounces late on pole-sitter Antonio Fuoco while Nicky Catsburg dominates GTE as Max Powers storms from last to the podium.
stories.body:
The rolling asphalt of Portimão does not ease a driver into a new racing season; it throws them straight into the tumult. Beneath the crisp autumn sun of southern Portugal, where the dry breeze off the Atlantic cuts across the undulating curves of the Autódromo Internacional do Algarve, the curtain came up on the Road to Glory championship with an electric 40-minute Prologue sprint. With points instantly on the line and no room for early-season hesitation, the opener delivered sheer tactical tension across both classes, setting immediate benchmarks and serving notice of what promises to be an unrelenting campaign.

## Conway Strikes Late in Algarve Thriller

For twenty-two laps, Antonio Fuoco looked untouchable. Placing the scarlet #50 Ferrari AF Corse 499P on pole with a blistering 1:37.023 in qualifying, the Italian launched into a commanding opening stint, carving through traffic and dictating the tempo from the drop of the green flag. Behind him, however, **Mike Conway** was playing the long game in the #7 Toyota Gazoo Racing GR010 Hybrid. Starting from fifth on the grid, Conway methodically dismantled the deficit, picking off Earl Bamber and Alessandro Pier Guidi before stalking the leaders into the pit window.

When the front-runners made their mandatory fuel stops on lap 16—Conway stationary for 54 seconds, Fuoco for 56—the gap evaporated. Although Fuoco retained net track position once intermediate leaders Loïc Duval and Kévin Estre completed their services, Conway applied relentless pressure. Armed with the fastest lap of the race at 1:37.428 and clocking an unrelenting 1:38.513 typical pace, Conway hunted down the Ferrari and seized the lead on lap 23 with a decisive move. Taking the checkered flag by 4.670 seconds, Conway pocketed maximum race points and the fastest-lap bonus to leave Portugal leading the Hypercar standings with 26 points. Fuoco settled for second and 20 points after leading 20 laps, while Duval held onto a remarkable third place for Peugeot TotalEnergies (+16.842s), delivering a hard-earned 15 points in the wingless 9X8. Sébastien Buemi fought through to fourth in the sister #8 Toyota, narrowly fending off Earl Bamber’s Cadillac V-Series.R by five hundredths of a second.

## Catsburg and Corvette Command LMGTE

While the Hypercar fight went right down to the penultimate lap, the battle for the LMGTE victory was defined by sheer, unblemished perfection. Nicky Catsburg delivered a clinic behind the wheel of the Corvette Racing #33 C8.R. After planting the yellow machine on pole with a lap of 1:45.983, the Dutchman simply disappeared. Managing tire degradation with extraordinary mechanical sympathy, Corvette Racing chose not to stop at all during the 40-minute sprint. Catsburg led every single one of the 23 laps, turning identical laps like clockwork—posting a median lap time of 1:47.839 with an astonishing standard deviation of just 0.39 seconds.

Catsburg crossed the line 43.069 seconds ahead of the chasing pack, scooping all 27 available points for the win, pole, and most laps led. The battle behind him, though, was frantic. Harry Tincknell unleashed furious raw speed in the #88 Proton Competition Porsche 911 RSR-19, punching in the fastest GTE lap of the race at 1:45.323. Pitting on lap 20 for fresh rubber and fuel, Tincknell rejoined with sufficient margin to claim a clear second place, earning 19 points to open his account. Yet the true drama of the production-based class unfolded directly behind them in an astonishing scramble up the order.

## The Charge: Powers Scales the Mountain

The drive of the day belonged squarely to human contender **Max Powers** in the #57 Kessel Racing Ferrari 488 GTE Evo. Starting from dead last in fourteenth after a troubled qualifying run, Powers faced a steep mountain on a circuit where passing requires absolute commitment. What followed was a breathtaking demonstration of racecraft. While rivals tangled or struggled for rhythm, Powers sliced forward lap after lap, cracking into the top ten by lap two and muscling his way into seventh before the halfway mark.

His march through the pack was anything but gentle. The Ferrari was pushed to the absolute edge, clocking an eye-opening top speed of 266.21 kph on the Algarve main straight—by far the fastest recorded in the GTE field. Along the way, Powers absorbed heavy contact: a hard hit (severity 901) with PJ Hyett’s Project 1 Porsche around the eleven-minute mark, and a massive collision with Hypercar contender Sébastien Buemi at minute 29.6 measuring a colossal 2312 severity as multi-class traffic converged into the heavy braking zones. Despite collecting a track limit warning in the heat of battle, Powers kept the 488 pointed straight.

Kessel Racing timed their strategy to perfection. Calling Powers in on lap 18 for a swift 39-second fuel-only stop, they avoided tyre changes and jumped directly ahead of the Porsche contingent—including Sarah Bovy, Michael Wainwright, and Christian Ried—when those squads took both fuel and rubber on lap 20. Powers cycled up to fourth, then picked off Luis Perez Companc’s non-stopping AF Corse Ferrari in the closing moments to secure a stunning third place. An eleven-position ascent netted Powers 15 championship points and a podium trophy that felt entirely improbable forty minutes earlier. Perez Companc held fourth ahead of Iron Dames driver Bovy.

## Foundations Laid for Long Beach

With the opening salvo concluded, the championship tables reflect a fascinating hierarchy. Mike Conway sits atop Hypercar on 26 points, flanked by Antonio Fuoco (20) and Loïc Duval (15), while Sébastien Buemi (12) and Earl Bamber (10) lurk within striking distance. In LMGTE, Nicky Catsburg’s imperious 27-point haul establishes Corvette as the early benchmark, but Harry Tincknell (19) and Max Powers (15) have staked their claim as genuine title contenders. Next up, the field crosses the Atlantic for the grueling Beach Endurance at Long Beach, where 80 minutes on the unforgiving California street course will test these early front-runners against concrete walls that offer no forgiveness.

stories.title: A New Dawn Beckons: Inside the 2023 Road to Glory Campaign
stories.standfirst: Six rounds of relentless multi-class warfare await as the world's finest prototypes and GT machines prepare to battle from Portimão to Spa.
stories.body:
There is a distinct, electric hum that settles over the pit lane when a brand-new season waits on the horizon. The liveries are immaculate, the carbon weave unblemished, and the ledger entirely blank. Ahead lies the 2023 Road to Glory championship, a six-round tour across the globe that promises to push machines and minds to their absolute limits. Multi-class endurance racing is never just about ultimate single-lap pace; it is an intricate dance of traffic management, stamina, and strategic daring. With two distinct categories sharing asphalt—the fire-breathing Hypercar prototypes and the fiercely contested production-based LMGTE machinery—every corner will be an exercise in spatial awareness and calculated aggression.

With an escalating points structure awarding up to 50 points to winners in the grueling 80-minute long-distance bouts, and 25 points on the line during the frantic 40-minute sprints, championship momentum can pivot in an afternoon. Added bonuses for pole position, fastest lap, and leading the most laps mean every fraction of a second matters from the moment pit lane green lights illuminate.

## The Battlegrounds: Six Steps Across the World

The campaign opens with a fast-paced sprint at the Autódromo Internacional do Algarve in Portimão. The Portuguese circuit is a rollercoaster of undulating blind crests and plunging drops, where drivers must commit wholeheartedly without always seeing the apex ahead. From the Algarve, the paddock crosses the Atlantic for an 80-minute trial by concrete at Long Beach. Street racing in multi-class machinery is a relentless test of discipline; the seaside Californian course offers zero margin for error, where a brush with the wall can wipe out an afternoon's work in an instant.

Round three heads to historical sanctuary: Imola. The Autodromo Internazionale Enzo e Dino Ferrari is narrow, bordered by vicious curbs, and unforgiving of overzealous overtakes. Surviving the Italian test leads into a bruising 40-minute sprint over the notorious bumps of Sebring International Raceway under evening skies. The weathered runways of Central Florida rattle suspensions and shake loose any mechanical vulnerability. Spain's Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya hosts the penultimate round—an 80-minute tactical marathon where tire preservation around the abrasive sweeping bends will reign supreme—before the grand finale at the cathedral of endurance racing: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps. The Ardennes forest will provide the ultimate dramatic curtain call through the sweeps of Eau Rouge and the Blanchimont flat-out sprint.

## The Hypercar Vanguard: Giants Collide

At the sharp end of the grid, the Hypercar division represents a breathtaking clash of philosophies. Toyota Gazoo Racing arrives with unmatched endurance pedigree, fielding the peerless GR010 Hybrids. The #7 entry anchored by Mike Conway, Kamui Kobayashi, and José María López, alongside the sister #8 of Sébastien Buemi, Brendon Hartley, and Ryo Hirakawa, set the gold standard in operational discipline.

Yet the Japanese powerhouse faces a red-liveried assault from Maranello. Ferrari AF Corse’s factory 499P prototypes—the #50 driven by Antonio Fuoco, Miguel Molina, and Nicklas Nielsen, and the #51 of Alessandro Pier Guidi, James Calado, and Antonio Giovinazzi—are poised to reclaim the Prancing Horse’s top-flight heritage. Porsche Penske Motorsport counters with the aggressive pair of 963 prototypes (#5 and #6), boasting established endurance stalwarts like Kévin Estre, Laurens Vanthoor, and André Lotterer. With customer entries from Hertz Team JOTA and Proton Competition reinforcing the Porsche fleet, alongside the roaring V8 of Cadillac Racing’s #2 V-Series.R, the avant-garde wingless Peugeot 9X8s, and spirited efforts from Glickenhaus and Vanwall, the outright fight will be a vicious, unrelenting affair.

## The Final Song of GTE: Pure Multi-Car Warfare

While prototypes hunt outright glory, the LMGTE field offers an intoxicating, elbow-to-elbow brawl that may well deliver the closest racing of the year. This marks the swan song era for the naturally aspirated shrieks and twin-turbo growls of pure GTE platforms, and the entry list is stacked with championship credentials.

Corvette Racing’s singular C8.R (#33), led by the ever-reliable Ben Keating and Nicky Catsburg, enters as an immediate benchmark on pace and operational consistency. Yet the Porsche 911 RSR-19 contingent is massive and lethal. The crowd-favorite Iron Dames (#85) lineup of Sarah Bovy, Rahel Frey, and Michelle Gatting proved time and again they can control a race from the front, while Dempsey-Proton (#77), Project 1 - AO (#56), and GR Racing (#86) bring deep technical experience to the table. Aston Martin’s trio of Vantage GTEs, headed by ORT by TF (#25) and NorthWest AMR (#98), are primed to exploit any high-speed circuit characteristics.

## Powers in the Spotlight: Kessel Racing’s Challenge

In the heart of this cutthroat GT arena sits **Max Powers**, strapping into the cockpit of the #57 Kessel Racing Ferrari 488 GTE Evo. Powers carries both the pride and pressure of representing the Swiss-based squad, sharing the stable’s lineage with veterans like Daniel Serra and Takeshi Kimura. The 488 GTE Evo is a refined, beautifully balanced weapon, renowned for its stability under heavy braking and gentle tire wear, which should pay enormous dividends on long stints like Long Beach and Barcelona.

For Powers, the mission is formidable. Running against factory-backed efforts and elite GT privateers on a 90 percent difficulty benchmark leaves no room for hesitation. Survival through the chaotic prototype traffic while keeping the #57 machine glued to the rear bumpers of the Corvettes and Porsches will test racecraft and calm nerve alike. If Powers can combine opportunistic overtaking with disciplined tire management across the opening skirmishes in Portimão and Long Beach, Kessel Racing could quickly emerge as a genuine thorn in the side of the established favorites. The engines are warming in the garages. Road to Glory is underway.
